profile.summary: Spec2Mol recommends molecular structures from tandem mass spectra (MS/MS) alone. An encoder turns a set of four spectra of a compound (positive and negative mode, low and high collision energy) into an embedding, and a decoder pretrained on about 135 million molecules turns that embedding into SMILES strings. It is modelled on speech-to-text systems.

summary_quotes.text: We propose Spec2Mol, a deep learning architecture for molecular structure recommendation given mass spectra alone.

The encoder learns the spectra embeddings, while the decoder, pre-trained on a massive dataset of chemical structures for translating between different molecular representations, reconstructs SMILES sequences of the recommended chemical structures.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The decoder comes from a SMILES autoencoder with GRU encoder and decoder, pretrained on about 135 million PubChem and ZINC-12 molecules to translate between molecular representations. The spectra encoder is trained to predict that autoencoder's embedding from four spectra per compound: [M+H]+ and [M-H]- precursors at 35% and 130% NCE. Structures are produced either directly, by sampling several SMILES from the decoder and keeping valid ones, or indirectly, by retrieving database structures close to the embedding.

sections.body: The repository holds one trained spectra encoder (spectra_encoder.pt) and the decoder model, vocabulary and config (decoder/models/), plus sample spectra and a sample embedding file. The encoder was trained on the NIST Tandem Mass Spectral Library 2020, a commercial dataset. facts.value: Spectra encoder (repository files model1D2Conv.py and spectra_encoder_model.py) predicting an embedding; GRU-based SMILES decoder from a pretrained autoencoder (translation model adapted from MOSES).

facts.label: Inputs
facts.value: Four spectra per compound as CSV files of m/z and intensity: [M+H]+ at 35% and 130% NCE, and [M-H]- at 35% and 130% NCE.

quotes.text: Each csv file has the m/z values in the first column and the intensity values in the second column.

facts.label: Outputs
facts.value: Spectra embeddings, then several SMILES per embedding (separated by |) in a CSV.

quotes.text: Multiple SMILES strings will be generated for each embedding and will be separated using the `|` symbol.

strengths.text: Weights for both the encoder and decoder are in the repository with sample inputs, under BSD-3-Clause.
The pretrained decoder reconstructs about 93.3% of NIST molecules from their embeddings (the authors' figure), so most errors come from the spectrum encoder.

quotes.text: The AE was able to correctly reconstruct the SMILES sequence for about 93.3% of the NIST molecules.

strengths.text: The authors report it can identify key substructures and performs on par with fragmentation tree methods when the test structure is not in the reference database (the authors' claim).

quotes.text: Spec2Mol is able to identify the presence of key molecular substructures from its mass spectrum

limitations.text: The released encoder expects four spectra per compound (two precursor types at two energies), which many datasets do not have.

run_guide.summary: Install Spec2Mol, compute an embedding for the bundled four-spectrum sample, and decode the sample embedding file into SMILES with the released decoder.
prerequisites: CUDA is recommended for the decoder; CPU is supported.
Four spectra per compound in the README's CSV format.

steps.title: Get the code
steps.shell:
git clone https://github.com/KavrakiLab/Spec2Mol.git
cd Spec2Mol
git checkout --detach 33dbcc4daaf53e30a5b5c437ef3275d6a5984ace
steps.explanation: Clone and pin the reviewed commit; these lines are added by Rewire.

steps.title: Install
steps.shell:
conda create -n spec2mol python=3.7
source activate spec2mol
conda install rdkit -c rdkit
conda install pytorch=1.6.0 torchvision -c pytorch

quotes.text: conda create -n spec2mol python=3.7 source activate spec2mol conda install rdkit -c rdkit conda install pytorch=1.6.0 torchvision -c pytorch

steps.title: Generate spectra embeddings
steps.explanation: The README's command for the sample spectra, with its trailing line-continuation removed.

steps.title: Decode embeddings to SMILES
steps.shell:
cd decoder
python -m scripts.decode_embeddings --output_file decoded_output.csv \
    --predicted_embeddings sample.pt \
    --model translation \
    --device cuda \
    --model_load models/model.pt \
    --vocab_load models/vocab.nb \
    --config_load models/config.nb \
    --n_batch 65 \
    --num_variants 3
steps.explanation: Decodes the provided sample embeddings; the paths in the decoder README are relative to the decoder folder, so Rewire added cd decoder. Use --device cpu without a GPU.

quotes.text: `device`: cuda or cpu. cuda is recommended

outputs: decoded_output.csv with several SMILES per embedding, separated by |.
limitations: These commands were read from the repository and have not been executed by Rewire.
